vision: Measure whether the existing CR Analyzer pipeline's risk signals predict real post-execution failures at statistical scale, using ApacheJIT (28K bug-inducing commits, Tier B labels) as the primary corpus. Deliver an adapter, temporal train/test evaluation harness, and honest documentation of what this proves vs what ITSM CAB validation still requires. Pipeline stages remain unchanged; only adapters, eval code, docs, and tests are added.
direction: Extend the adapter pattern established by BPI 2014 (`src/cr_analyzer/adapters/bpi2014.py`) with a new ApacheJIT adapter that maps Zenodo CSV rows to CRBundle objects plus external ground-truth labels. Use the dataset's built-in temporal splits (`apachejit_train.csv` for 2003–2016, `apachejit_test_large.csv` for 2017+). Build incident_history chronologically per project from prior buggy commits (no future leakage). Add a separate predictive eval module under `src/cr_analyzer/eval/` (distinct from architecture eval in `evaluate.py`) that runs the unchanged pipeline on the test split, derives risk scores from CabReport outputs, and reports precision/recall/F1/AUC/confusion matrix. Document the semantic gap between bug-inducing commits and ITSM incident-causing changes. All 147 existing tests plus BPI adapter must keep passing.

cleanup.breadcrumbs_policy: Archive full history to archive/phases/, then start a fresh append-only trail. Rationale: 64 lines span two completed phases; a clean trail makes session resume unambiguous. Historical trace lives in the archived copy.

trade_offs.decision: ApacheJIT as primary predictive corpus (not BPI 2014 outcome linkage)
trade_offs.alternative: Extend BPI adapter for Related Change → incident ground truth (n=25 P1/P2)
trade_offs.reasoning: BPI 2014 validates architecture (done) but lacks statistical power for precision/recall. ApacheJIT offers 28K positives with built-in temporal splits. We accept Tier B (SZZ+JIRA) label noise and domain shift from ITSM.

trade_offs.decision: No pipeline code changes — eval-side scoring only
trade_offs.alternative: Add completeness bypass flag for partial bundles
trade_offs.reasoning: User constraint: pipeline unchanged. ApacheJIT bundles lack runbook/rollback/comms, so completeness will emit blocker findings and full-pipeline recommendation will skew reject-heavy. Eval harness reports BOTH full-pipeline metrics (baseline, expected degenerate) AND completeness-excluded risk scores for meaningful AUC/threshold analysis.

trade_offs.decision: Project-level incident_history from prior buggy commits (not file-level)
trade_offs.alternative: Re-fetch GitHub diffs for file overlap with historical buggy commits
trade_offs.reasoning: Zenodo CSV has metrics (LA/LD/NF/ND/NS/ENT) but not file paths or commit messages. Project-scoped chronological buggy-commit history activates Historical Pattern stage with honest data available. File-level history would require GitHub API enrichment — defer to open question.

trade_offs.decision: Synthetic description when commit message absent from CSV
trade_offs.alternative: Mandatory GitHub API fetch for every commit message
trade_offs.reasoning: Standard ApacheJIT CSV columns are commit_id, project, buggy, fix, year, author_date, and change metrics — no message column. Adapter uses structured placeholder (project + commit_id + key metrics) so pipeline runs without network dependency. Optional enrichment path documented, not required for P0.
Predictive benchmarking requires reproducibility and cost control. L1 is deterministic and matches architecture eval baseline. L2 comparison can be a follow-up task after L1 numbers exist.

trade_offs.decision: Separate eval module (`predictive_eval.py`) from architecture eval (`evaluate.py`)
trade_offs.reasoning: Architecture eval (BPI CAB windows, L1 vs L2, disposition breakdown) and predictive eval (ground truth, confusion matrix, AUC) serve different questions. Separation keeps each harness focused and avoids regressing BPI eval tests.

open_questions: Commit message enrichment: fetch from GitHub by commit_id for richer description/Historical Pattern L2, or stay CSV-only for P0?
Eval scale: run full test_large (~30K commits, hours) or default to test_small (~3K) with full run documented as manual step?
Primary score for AUC threshold sweep: completeness-excluded weighted finding score, recommendation ordinal, or historical-pattern-only findings?
Should train split be used only for history context (chronological prior) or also for pipeline calibration — noting pipeline has no trainable weights today?
Report negative result honestly if completeness-excluded scores show no signal — is that an adapter problem or expected domain gap?
